work.text: He relates an incident which happened at a large entertainment given to [distinguished] guests at the Enryokwan when he with two other painters were engaged to amuse the assembly by making paintings. Commencing about the middle of the day [Kyōsai] made over a hundred paintings in eight hours.

source.author: Josiah Conder
source.title: Paintings and Studies by Kawanabé Kyōsai

work.lead: His pupil Josiah Conder, from Kyōsai’s own account:

moment.text: In this collaborative painting, artists create works in response to patrons’ requests. Kawanabe Kyōsai painted the figures and outlines of the screens and scrolls, and 10 bunjin completed them.
Physician and calligrapher Nakane Hanrei (中根半嶺) (1831–1914) wrote “longevity” (壽) with an enormous ink-filled brush.

matters.text: In the former case, should there be any fault in his paintings, it would be excusable, as they were made as a pastime for the guests, but the pictures deliberately carried out in his studio were his life’s work, to remain as evidence of the extent of his powers
